title: How login works (OAuth 2.0 + PKCE)
summary: The browser never holds a token. It runs the OAuth redirect dance with Auth0, then hands the one-time code to a small **auth gateway**. The gateway swaps the code for tokens, keeps them in Redis, and gives the browser an opaque session cookie.

bff.desc: Backend-for-frontend. It's the only component that sees access and refresh tokens, and it attaches them to API calls on the browser's behalf.

sessions.desc: Maps `sid` to `{ access_token, refresh_token, expires_at }`. The TTL matches the refresh token lifetime.

idp.desc: Auth0 tenant. It hosts the login page, MFA and social logins. The app never sees a password.

steps.say: You click **Log in**. The web app creates a random `code_verifier` and keeps it in memory. Only its SHA-256 hash leaves the browser.
The browser is redirected to Auth0 with the hashed challenge and a `state` value for CSRF protection.
You sign in on Auth0's page, with password, passkey or Google, plus MFA if it's enabled. The web app is not involved at this point.
Auth0 redirects back with a short-lived, single-use **authorization code**. On its own the code is useless: whoever redeems it must also present the original verifier.
The web app sends the code and the verifier to the auth gateway.
The gateway redeems the code. Auth0 hashes the verifier and checks it against the challenge from step 2, so a stolen code can't be redeemed by anyone else.
Auth0 returns a 15-minute access token and a refresh token.
The gateway stores both tokens in Redis under a random session id.
The browser only receives an `HttpOnly` cookie. JavaScript can't read it, so an XSS bug can't leak a token.

flows.label: Call the API
flows.description: What happens on every request after login, including the silent refresh.

steps.say: The web app calls its own origin. The cookie is sent automatically.
The gateway looks up the session. If the access token expires within 60 seconds, it refreshes it first by sending the refresh token to Auth0.
The gateway forwards the request with the access token. The Products API only validates JWTs and knows nothing about cookies or sessions.

next: To add a new protected API, route it through the gateway. Services behind it only need to verify the JWT signature and the `aud` claim.
To log a user out everywhere, delete their `sid:*` keys in Redis and revoke the refresh token in Auth0.
To debug a login loop, check that the `state` and the cookie `SameSite` setting survive the redirect back from Auth0.
